title: Cornell says ex-US Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates will investigate school’s response to Jane Doe’s rape allegations | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A former Justice Department official will delve into Cornell University’s response to a student’s allegations of gang rape as outrage over the case echoes across the country – fromsexual abuse survivorsto students on campus and now to the school’s president.

Former US Deputy Attorney General Sally Q. Yates will lead an independent review of how Cornell “prevents and responds to sexual harassment, sexual assault and related misconduct on campus,”the university saidTuesday.

That review will include “whether Cornell followed its policies and procedures in responding to” sexual assault allegations brought by a student, known as Jane Doe, against members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024, the university said.

An attorney for one of the students named in Doe’s lawsuit on Tuesday said he and his client “welcome” the decision to have an independent review of Cornell University’s handling of the sexual assault investigation.

“We think an independent review is appropriate. Sally Yates has tremendous experience as a prosecutor and investigator, and she and her team should have access to the full record and the freedom to follow the facts wherever they lead,” Andrew Miltenberg said in a statement to CNN.

He added that the university should be held to the same standard it expects of students.

“We support the review and hope it provides an objective assessment of what happened and, where appropriate, what Cornell can do better. At the end of the day, the facts should speak for themselves,” Miltenberg said.

The announcement came after members of Cornell’s Faculty Senate introduced a resolution Monday evening calling for a vote of no confidence against the administration. A vote of no confidence is a formal rebuke of a group’s leadership – and often an attempt to force change or compel resignations.

“The faculty have been approached by hundreds of students, alumni, staff who are demanding that we do something,” labor history professor and Faculty Senate member Paul Ortiz told CNN. Some of the students who have approached faculty said they had endured sexual assault, Ortiz said.

“We’re tired of the sexual assaults that happened to our students,” he said. “We’re tired of the administration’s inaction on this issue – and not only our current students, but past students, alumni who have actually given money to this university are fed up.”

Students and community members rallied through streets in Ithaca on Monday evening, chanting “shame” and “resign” after details of the rape allegations came to light in a recently filed civil lawsuit from the former student.

Some groups are also planning to host a seven-hour sit-in on Wednesday “in solidarity with Jane Doe,” according to social media flyers for the event.

The lawsuit Doe filed last month against the university, the Chi Phi fraternity, seven fraternity members and others alleges the school failed to protect her and adequately punish the accused students. Doe has received threats since the lawsuit came to light, her attorney said.

The ensuing fallout has raised questions about how Cornell police handled Jane Doe’s allegations, how much information was shared with the district attorney’s office, the prosecutors’ initial decision not to file charges, and whether the school’s internal investigation and actions went far enough.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Kara Scannell, Taylor Galgano, Danya Gainor, Isa Mudannayake and Cindy Von Quednow contributed to this report.
